newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Handlowy rates Wedel as "hold".
newsitem.headline: Polish Handlowy rates Wedel as "hold".

text.p: The brokerage unit of Polish Bank Handlowy SA advised investors to hold shares in confectioner Wedel SA, saying it had strong market position but was facing increasing competition in its sector.
Handlowy said in its report dated January 3, but released on Monday, Wedel's strategic investor PepsiCo, which in 83-percent controls the company guaranteed the firm's growth.
The report noted an extensive $150 million investment programme for 1997-2000 and Wedel's expansion in the high margin salty snacks segment.
But it expected Wedel could be losing market share in some market segments because of increasing competition from international companies.

"However, it should be taken into account that the increasing competition on the domestic market will have an influence on a weakening of the company's position in some segments of the market," it said.

It also said an unresolved dispute with heirs of the company's founder, who claim the right to the firm's name cast a cloud on the company's future as the high brand recognition on the domestic market was one of its key assets.
Handlowy expected Wedel's net profit to roise to 55 million zlotys on 858-million-zloty-sales, up from last year's 40.8-million and 650.1-million respectively.
Wedel closed at 147 zlotys on Friday.
